legal system is vast, complex and fluid, and legal knowledge is difficult for lay citizens to access or interpret amid\u2002thousands of statutes, millions of judgments, and constantly evolving legislation. Although LLMs can produce elegant answers, they often hallucinate\u2002in the legal domain and are not able to cite authoritative sources reliably. We introduce a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based approach specifically designed for the Indian legal domain, supported by a large structured legal corpus of 45\u201360 million tokens and a sentence-aware chunking mechanism for creating text embeddings using Instructor-XL, integrating FAISS HNSW for retrieval and GPT-4o for grounded generation. The platform delivers natural-language legal answers with citations and context to help bring legal knowledge\u2002into the general populace and enable greater public access to justice. We present the architecture, dataset construction, retrieval pipeline, evaluation methodology, and responsible-AI\u2002aspects for robust deployment of legal-domain RAG systems in
